title: Kind of Blue
blurb: Six musicians, a handful of sketched-out scales, and two sessions. The best selling jazz record ever made.

title: A Love Supreme
blurb: A four-part suite recorded in a single December session, and a devotional statement as much as an album.

title: Blue Train
blurb: Coltrane's only session as a leader for Blue Note, cut in one night with a sextet firing on all cylinders.

title: Saxophone Colossus
blurb: Rollins at twenty-five, playing with a swagger and a sense of structure that nobody had matched yet.

title: My Favorite Things
blurb: A show tune turned into a soprano saxophone incantation that runs almost fourteen minutes.

title: Song for My Father
blurb: The bossa-inflected title track has been sampled and borrowed so often you already know the piano vamp.

title: Mingus Ah Um
blurb: Gospel, blues, and elegy shoved together by a bassist who wrote like a composer and led like a bandleader.

title: Head Hunters
blurb: Four tracks, a Fender Rhodes, and a clavinet riff that rewired what a jazz record was allowed to sound like.

title: Maiden Voyage
blurb: An oceanic concept record built on suspended chords that never quite resolve where you expect.

title: Giant Steps
blurb: The title track cycles through three keys a major third apart and has terrified saxophonists ever since.

title: Time Out
blurb: An experiment in odd time signatures that accidentally produced one of the best known tunes in jazz.

title: Bitches Brew
blurb: Electric, sprawling, and edited together from long studio jams. Purists hated it; everyone else followed.
